note: The three session.start capability reports (collaboration spec §5.6). Each field is OPTIONAL PERMANENTLY. A reader returns three answers — absent / recorded / malformed — and absence means "this recorder does not report", never "the capability was missing".
absence_note: no_capability_reports is the pre-§5.6 payload and is the hash every 1.x session.start of this shape already has. Compare it against git_capture_available to see that a report changes the bytes, and against git_capture_null_is_not_absent to see that null and omission are different bytes despite reading the same.
not_a_knob_note: These are CAPABILITY REPORTS, not capture knobs. A capability report says "I could not"; a knob says "I was told not to". Nothing here appears in policy.capture, nothing here is course-signed, and nothing here is ever a finding — no flag, no validation check, no severity, no score.
git_capture_note: unavailable = the editor exposed no git integration, so no git.event could be produced at all. not_owned = git observation worked and no repository it could see was in this assignment's scope, so its events were dropped by the ownership gate. These are different situations a grader acts on differently and MUST NOT be collapsed. available = git observation was live.
witness_capture_note: Two values, deliberately. There is no witnessing analogue of not_owned: a recorder witnesses the .provenance/ directory it is itself writing into, so there is no ownership question to route on.
file_scope_note: The RESOLVED LIST, not the rule. A count cannot be asked whether it contains a file, and publishing an unresolved glob set would require three hand-written ports and one analyzer to agree on a matcher. Paths are assignment-root-relative, exactly as every other path in the log. complete:false means the list is a strict subset, and a path's absence from it is then UNKNOWN rather than NOT WATCHED.
file_scope_privacy_note: S14(b) forbids repository paths and remote URLs. An absolute path (POSIX, Windows drive or UNC), any colon (which is every remote-URL spelling, including git’s scp-style user@host:path) and any ".." segment are rejected — and a single bad entry rejects the WHOLE set, because a silently narrowed list says "not watched" about a file that was.
writer_note: OMIT a field you cannot answer. Never emit null: the two canonicalize differently and therefore chain to different hashes, exactly as `parents: []` and an absent `parents` do. Readers accept null as absence so a nonconforming log still parses; a writer that emits it is nonconforming.

cases.name: no_capability_reports
cases.note: The pre-§5.6 payload, and every bundle in existence. All three read absent, and this hash is unchanged by the fields existing in the format.

cases.name: git_capture_available
cases.note: Git observation was live. An absence of git.event in this session is a statement about git activity, not about capture.

cases.name: git_capture_unavailable
cases.note: No git integration on this machine. Nothing this session did could have produced a git.event.

cases.name: git_capture_not_owned
cases.note: Git worked; no repository it could see was in scope. NOT the same fact as unavailable, and a reader that reports one as the other describes a different situation than the one that occurred.

cases.name: git_capture_null_is_not_absent
cases.note: Reads as absence, and hashes differently from no_capability_reports. A writer must OMIT.

cases.name: git_capture_unknown_value_rejected
cases.note: Outside the closed enum. Malformed, counted, never a finding, and never presented as a capability.

cases.name: git_capture_uppercase_rejected
cases.note: Case is not folded: folding would be exactly the normalization the reader refuses.

cases.name: git_capture_not_a_string_rejected
cases.note: A non-string value is malformed rather than coerced.

cases.name: witness_capture_available
cases.note: A .provenance/ watcher was running. Had a partner log appeared, changed or vanished, this session would have witnessed it.

cases.name: witness_capture_unavailable
cases.note: No watcher. The absence of peer.observed in this session says nothing about what was in .provenance/.

cases.name: witness_capture_not_owned_rejected
cases.note: git_capture's third value is not legal here. A port that shares one enum between the two fields fails this case.

cases.name: witness_capture_null_is_not_absent
cases.note: Reads as absence, hashes differently from omission.

cases.name: file_scope_complete
cases.note: The effective resolved file set. A path NOT in a complete list was not watched, which is what makes "no events for this file" unambiguous.

cases.name: file_scope_empty_is_a_real_answer
cases.note: The scope resolved to nothing. A positive claim that explains every file’s silence — not absence, and not to be folded into it.

cases.name: file_scope_truncated
cases.note: The list is a strict subset. A path in it WAS watched; a path not in it is UNKNOWN, never "not watched".

cases.name: file_scope_missing_complete_rejected
cases.note: complete is required and is never inferred — the field exists to remove an inference.

cases.name: file_scope_not_an_object_rejected
cases.note: An array is not a file scope; the list lives under `watched`.

cases.name: file_scope_absolute_path_rejected
cases.note: S14(b). An absolute path embeds the account name and the machine layout. The WHOLE set is rejected, not just this entry.

cases.name: file_scope_windows_path_rejected
cases.note: A Windows drive path is absolute too. A port that only checks for a leading "/" fails this case.

cases.name: file_scope_remote_url_rejected
cases.note: S14(b). A remote URL embeds the org and frequently the student’s own username.

cases.name: file_scope_scp_remote_rejected
cases.note: git’s scp-style remote has no "://" and is still a remote URL. The rule is any colon outside a Windows drive letter.

cases.name: file_scope_parent_escape_rejected
cases.note: A ".." segment names something outside the assignment scope.

cases.name: file_scope_dotted_names_accepted
cases.note: Paths that merely LOOK risky are ordinary: a leading dot, a doubled dot inside a segment, and backslash separators are all accepted verbatim.

cases.name: file_scope_unknown_extra_key_accepted
cases.note: Forward compatibility: a newer recorder adding a key must not make this reader refuse the whole scope.

cases.name: file_scope_null_is_not_absent
cases.note: Reads as absence, hashes differently from omission.

cases.name: all_three_reported
cases.note: The shape a §5.6-conformant recorder emits when it can answer all three. The three fields are independent: a port may land one before the others.
